body:
incidents-bot: [PAGER] latency SLO alerts in eu-west-1 — p95 > 600ms for /v1/generate. Automated routing decisions observed. Pager level: P2. (12:03 UTC)

oncall-frontend: paging @sre-jordan @ml-infra-lee — looks like multiple reroutes happening, could be smart-routing churn

sre-jordan: oncall here, joining. pulling traces and routing logs now

ml-infra-lee: I see a lot of routing_policy->fallback events. Services flip between variants: gptx-stable-v2 <-> gptx-quant-small every ~30s. CPU & tail latency spike after fallback.

sre-jordan: can you paste the policy blob that's causing fallbacks?

ml-infra-lee: here's the relevant config snippet:```json
{"policy":"latency_slo","threshold_ms":500,"cooldown_seconds":60,"fallback":"auto_variant","criteria":["p95","seq_len"]}
```

sre-jordan: cooldown 60s is shorter than observed oscillation period. If p95 spikes for 30s it flips back and forth.

support-ana: inbound customer reports: 3 separate customers in EU reporting "generation much slower". No 5xxs, just high latency.

eng-oncall: quick mitigation proposal: disable smart-routing in eu-west-1 and pin endpoints to region-stable variant. This will stop churn but reduce headroom.

ops-jen: preparing rollout: will set routing.policy.enabled=false for eu-west-1 and pin to gptx-stable-v2. Deploy job queued (cmd: `./deploy routing-config --region eu-west-1 --set disabled`)

incidents-bot: deploy job started by ops-jen (job id: d-8793). Notifying observers.

ml-infra-lee: note — the auto_variant selection tends to pick the quantized smaller model under short-sequence signals; that variant handles latency poorly at our current batching distribution leading to per-token slowdown. Combined with short cooldown causes oscillation.

sre-jordan: doing a short-term mitigation: increase cooldown to 300s and temporarily disable auto fallback while we stabilize.

ops-jen: applied change: cooldown -> 300s, smart-routing disabled. Rolling config change now.

incidents-bot: update: mitigations applied. p95 trending down from ~800ms to ~220ms in eu-west-1 (monitoring window 5m).

product-sam: any estimate of customer impact/time window we should share?

support-ana: impact window ~12:03–12:47 UTC. Affected requests had 2-3x latency increase. Top 3 customers in EU experienced degraded UX. Tickets updated; contacting account owners.

eng-oncall: monitoring infra and capacity. CPU on a subset of pods spiked after the wrong variant was chosen, causing queueing and longer tail latencies.

ml-infra-lee: quick root-cause hypothesis: routing policy evaluated only p95, not utilization or in-flight batch size. With our batching distribution the smaller quantized variant becomes a bottleneck under medium load, increasing p95 and triggering another fallback.

sre-jordan: action items logged here: 1) short term: mitigation done 2) mid term: routing policy to require 3 consecutive windows under threshold before flip and include CPU util metric 3) long term: augment model-variants metadata with throughput profile for decisioning.

ops-jen: cooldown change confirmed; config hashes: old: `a7f3` new: `b2c9`. Rolling revert plan ready.

incidents-bot: status -> mitigated (monitoring). Please acknowledge before handoff.

eng-oncall: leaving pager; handing to SRE for ongoing watch for 2 hours. @sre-jordan taking over.

sre-jordan: acknowledged. I'll run a controlled canary to re-enable smart-routing with hysteresis: require 3 consecutive 60s buckets under SLO and CPU<70% before allowing variant switch. Also will add a 5-minute cooldown floor.

ml-infra-lee: will add a postmortem note to include a small simulation to validate policy under different batching patterns. Also propose adding utilization-aware selectors.

product-sam: draft customer message: "We observed routing instability in our EU region that caused elevated latencies for a subset of requests between 12:03–12:47 UTC. We have applied mitigations and are monitoring. A post-incident review is underway." Happy to send once SRE approves.

support-ana: customer comms sent to top impacted accounts; no escalations so far. :thumbsup:

sre-jordan: marking incident as mitigated->monitoring. Will own postmortem and timeline. Next steps: schedule postmortem, update runbook to add hysteresis and util checks, add automated tests for policy simulations.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT LOGGED: follow-up required. Runbook reference: /runbooks/routing-fallback-hysteresis.md. Please file postmortem in #postmortems within 48h.

eng-oncall: thanks team — leaving thread.

support-ana: closing customer tickets if no further reports.

sre-jordan: final note: avoid toggling smart-routing via quick fixes; prefer staged canary and smoke tests in region. Leaving monitoring.
